answer: Price each new identity by how many accounts already share its funding trail: the nth account from one source pays a burned joining fee of n squared. Like a vine that strangles itself, a farm of k clones pays about k cubed over three, while an honest newcomer pays one unit. Burned copper cannot be pooled or refunded, and tracing funds through a violet-flagged mixer only merges the trail, so splitting sources costs more than it saves.
